Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets

Rafael — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying Qs so we can finalize the PoC scope:

- Goal: real-time underwriting assistant for our trading desk (low-latency scoring + streaming rationale).
- Traffic profile (baseline): ~120 agents using the tool during market hours (9:30–16:00 ET).
- Expected steady-state: ~450 requests/minute; peak: up to 1,200 requests/minute during volatility.
- Each request: prompt ~700 tokens in, expected model output ~200–400 tokens streamed back.
- Target latency SLA: 95th perc < 300ms for first token, streaming tail within 2s for full rationale.

Clarifying Qs we discussed that I wanted in writing:
1) What throughput numbers should we size for to hit 95th <300ms with streaming enabled?
2) What concurrency/QPS assumptions drive autoscale and cost estimates?
3) Any constraints around tokenization or prompt-side batching we should be aware of?

I'll loop in Victor (infra) for capacity questions. Can you send a short sizing sheet we can share with our infra team?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jones
Director, Trading Infrastructure
Finex Corp

Quick answers up front:
- We'll prepare a short throughput estimate (tokens/sec, QPS, concurrency) today and attach a CSV with assumptions.
- Streaming: we can optimize first-token latency and maintain low end-to-end streaming tail by tuning kv-cache and enabling aggressive prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
- Batching: given you have relatively long prompts and streaming requirements, we'll propose small, latency-optimized batch sizes (1–4) for market-path calls and larger batching for async scoring jobs.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the sizing sheet with three scenarios (steady, peak, extreme burst).

Attaching initial estimate.

Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up — Finex proofpoint (tokens/sec, QPS)

Hi Sara — attaching the throughput_estimate.csv with conservative and aggressive scenarios and the assumptions used to calculate tokens/sec and QPS. Summary below:

- Steady state: 450 req/min => 7.5 req/sec; avg tokens per req (in+out) = 1,000 => ~7.5k tokens/sec.
- Peak: 1,200 req/min => 20 req/sec => ~20k tokens/sec.
- Extreme burst (10x short spikes): up to 200 req/sec => ~200k tokens/sec — recommend short-term autoscale + buffer pool.

Concurrency assumptions: average response streams are ~250 tokens emitted over ~1.2s; concurrent open streams at peak estimate ~40–60 (clients with long-polling).

Latency guidance (95th-first-token):
- For steady: single-instance (high-clock GPU) 95th ~120–200ms; with small batching (2–4) we still expect <250ms.
- For peak: multi-instance with autoscale target QPS/node ~25–40, 95th ~200–350ms depending on model and quantization.

Notes: these numbers assume a 7B-class open model with optimized kernels and int8 quantization. If Finex prefers a larger model (13B+), sizing and latency SLOs change significantly.

Please review and mark which scenario you want us to price for PoC. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow with Victor to walk the infra assumptions.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Victor Chu <victor.chu@finex.com>

Marissa — helpful spreadsheet, thanks. A couple of infra clarifications from my side:
1) Network egress: our corp policy requires predictable egress and we prefer VPC peering for the PoC. Any additional latency knock from peering?
2) KV cache warm-up: what warm-up timeline do you assume for prefix cache? During market open we may see rapid changes in prompts.
3) Autoscale: can we provision a buffer pool to handle 10–20% above peak without triggering cold starts?

Also — on the model choice: we want to start with the 7B to validate functionally, but keep the option to switch to 13B for higher-quality explanations after the PoC. How disruptive is that switch to the rollout plan?

Thanks,
Victor
VP, Core Infra
Finex Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Victor Chu <victor.chu@finex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up — Finex proofpoint (tokens/sec, QPS)

Victor — quick answers to your infra questions:

1) VPC peering adds minimal additional latency (typical 2–10ms), but we should test RTT in your target region. We'll include an e2e latency runbook in the PoC scope.
2) KV cache warm-up: for repeated system prompts we see effective prefix cache benefits within minutes; for rapidly changing prompts, cache hit-rate will be lower and we recommend a short cold-start plan (pre-warm samples at market open).
3) Buffer pool: yes — we can provision a warmed standby pool sized for ~20% above expected peak; that pool absorbs spikes without cold-starts (cost vs buffer trade-off discussed in the pricing memo).

Model switch: moving from 7B to 13B is supported as a model variant. Rollout path: start with 7B canonical for PoC, validate correctness/throughput, then do a canary switch to 13B with reduced traffic. It requires additional capacity (about ~2x TFLOPs) and we should plan the cost delta up front.

Action items from Redwood:
- Rafael/Marissa: confirm which scenario Finex wants priced for the PoC (steady/peak/extreme).
- We'll add a short runbook for peering RTT tests and cache warm-up steps to the Drive link.

Cheers,
Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
